caption: Earning US dollars with RefineryLens
say: This is how RefineryLens earns US dollars. Everything shown is demo data.

caption: Cargo benchmarks stop at the jetty. RefineryLens prices the street.
say: Price agencies already value West African fuel cargoes at the Lagos jetty. What nobody sells is what petrol, diesel and cooking gas actually cost on the street, in every Nigerian state. RefineryLens collects exactly that, every day, from households and sellers.

caption: Sold to traders, banks, multinationals and clean-cooking projects
say: So we sell it as data: to commodity traders, banks and development lenders, multinationals budgeting fuel, and clean-cooking projects.

caption: Medians from at least three reporters, never one person's price
say: Each figure is a median from at least three people or three sellers, with its range and reporter count. No single price, and no personal data, is ever sold.

caption: Plans in US dollars: $49, $299, and Enterprise from $1,500 a month
say: Plans are priced in US dollars. Starter is forty-nine dollars a month, Professional two hundred and ninety-nine, and Enterprise, with a licence to redistribute, from fifteen hundred.

caption: A documented REST API
say: The API is documented: four endpoints, clear limits and clear errors.

caption: A trading firm in Geneva signs up
say: Let's be a trading firm in Geneva. They create an account.

caption: A 14-day free trial, billed from Switzerland, so in dollars
say: They start a fourteen-day free trial. Billing from Switzerland means they pay in dollars. A Nigerian customer would pay the naira price, as the central bank's rules require.

caption: An API key, shown once and stored only as a hash
say: They create an API key. It is shown once, and RefineryLens stores only a scrambled copy.

caption: Calling the API with the new key
say: With that key, their systems get today's figures for every state as JSON, with the plan's allowance in the headers.

caption: Upgrade by card in dollars through Stripe or Paystack USD
say: To keep access after the trial, they pay by card in dollars, through Stripe or Paystack's US dollar service. On this demo neither is switched on yet, so the page says to ask for an invoice.

caption: Sponsored placements, sold in dollars and always labelled
say: The second dollar line is sponsorship. Equipment makers, like a CNG conversion firm, pay for a clearly labelled card where their customers are looking.

caption: Admin: data customers and recurring revenue in US dollars
say: On the admin side, data customers shows recurring revenue in dollars and in naira, kept apart, and every account with its usage.

caption: Enterprise deals: set the plan once the invoice is paid
say: When the Geneva firm signs an Enterprise contract and pays the invoice, we set their plan for the year.

caption: Add a sponsorship: placements, states, dates and the price in dollars
say: A new sponsor is added with its placements, target states, dates and the price in dollars. Views and clicks are counted for the sponsor's report.

caption: Payments: naira and dollar revenue, never added together
say: Payments show naira and dollar revenue on separate charts, never added together at a guessed exchange rate.

caption: Health: which dollar payment routes are switched on
say: And system health shows which dollar payment routes are switched on, and what each still needs.

caption: RefineryLens: Nigerian street prices, sold to the world in US dollars
say: RefineryLens. Nigerian street prices, sold to the world, in US dollars.
